key_insight: RL post-training gains in these LLMs are highly concentrated in a few transformer layers—often a single middle layer can recover most of the benefit of full-parameter training.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a much cheaper and more targeted RL fine-tuning strategy, reducing compute and memory while preserving most of the performance improvement.
method: Train one transformer layer at a time during RL post-training
Measure "layer contribution" as the fraction of full RL improvement recovered
Compare layer rankings across models, tasks, and RL algorithms
evidence_signal: Across seven models, two Qwen families, three RL algorithms, and multiple domains, the abstract reports a stable concentration of RL gains in middle layers with strong cross-setting correlation.
watch_item: Layer importance may depend on model family, task, and algorithm, so isolating a single layer could underperform if the target domain shifts or requires broader adaptation.
paper_title: Is One Layer Enough? Training A Single Transformer Layer Can Match Full-Parameter RL Training
